subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls fail closed for every legacy ownerless session row, or must OpenClaw provide an explicit migration or operator-adoption path first?
rationale: Ownerless rows have no provable plugin authority, but unconditional rejection can stop previously working plugin-runtime workflows after upgrade; repository policy requires maintainers to own that security-versus-compatibility boundary.

options.title: Fail closed explicitly
options.body: Reject ownerless rows, document the upgrade impact in the PR context, and require deployed proof for owner-owned, foreign-owned, and ownerless cases.

options.title: Add operator adoption
options.body: Provide a deliberate doctor or administrative migration that assigns ownership before plugin-runtime mutation is permitted.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access temporarily
options.body: Reject foreign-owned rows now but retain ownerless access under a named, tested, and time-bounded compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Fail closed explicitly
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows, document the upgrade impact in the PR context, and require deployed proof for owner-owned, foreign-owned, and ownerless cases.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the session-accessor serialization boundary makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the lifecycle and upgrade-policy decision.
